functionalHeader: Extra comments / Advising rules you MUST follow
functionalRows: Advising Student
view the name and GUC email of my assigned advisor
Normal Student / Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator / Administrator
view a student's current weekly schedule including course code, course name, lecture, tutorial and lab times and locations

A Normal Student may view only their own processed standard schedule. An Advising Student may view their own completed draft after an Advisor or Coordinator marks it Ready for Student Review, and may continue to view the final processed schedule. A completed draft has every required course and lecture, tutorial and lab slot assigned, has no blocking validation issue, and is not yet final. Incomplete drafts remain hidden from the student. Advisors and Coordinators may view an advising student's draft, review-ready or processed schedule, and Administrators have read-only access. The schedule is displayed as a weekly calendar and shows days off.
Normal Student / Advising Student
view my registered courses, the credit hours of each course and my total registered credit hours
Normal Student / Advising Student
select a registered course and view its assigned lecture, tutorial and lab details
Normal Student
view eligible destination group numbers and their complete weekly schedules for a whole-schedule swap

Show only standard schedule groups for the same term whose registered course-code set exactly matches the student's subjects, with no additional or missing subject. Display each group number and its complete lecture, tutorial and lab schedule.
Normal Student
submit a whole-schedule swap request by selecting one or more desired group numbers before the deadline

The system auto-populates the student's current group number and complete current schedule from the processed record; the student cannot edit them. The student selects one or more eligible desired groups and may have only one active swap request.
Normal Student
view open whole-schedule swap requests that I am eligible to complete

A request is visible only when the viewer's current group is one of the requester's desired groups, both students have the exact same registered course-code set and term, and both schedules are processed. Show the requester's current group, complete schedule and desired group options, but do not reveal the requester's identity.
Normal Student
complete an eligible open whole-schedule swap request and move into the requester's current group

Immediately before completion, revalidate the deadline, request status, desired-group membership, exact subject match, term and both processed schedules. Then atomically exchange the two students' group assignments and every lecture, tutorial and lab slot. Do not apply a partial swap or change either student's registered subjects. Only the first valid completion may succeed.
Normal Student
view my submitted or completed whole-schedule swap requests, their group details and statuses
Statuses are Open, Completed, Withdrawn and Expired.
Normal Student
withdraw my own open whole-schedule swap request
A completed, withdrawn or expired request cannot be withdrawn.
Advising Student
request a change to one assigned lecture, tutorial or lab slot in my completed schedule before it is processed and include an optional preference note

This action is available only while the completed schedule is Ready for Student Review and before the advising deadline. The request identifies the course, component type and current slot. The preference note may mention a preferred group or day. The student cannot directly change the slot.
Advising Student
view my slot-change requests, their statuses and the Advisor or Coordinator response
Statuses are Pending, Approved, Rejected and Withdrawn. The response identifies any approved replacement slot.
Advising Student
withdraw my pending slot-change request
Only a Pending request may be withdrawn. A request that has already been approved, rejected or withdrawn cannot be withdrawn again.
Normal Student / Advising Student
download or print my processed schedule
Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator
view a student's academic history organized into completed courses with grades, current courses and remaining courses

Show the student's Advisor, major, GPA, completed hours and current semester. Every remaining course shows its credit hours, prerequisites and offering season. An Advising Student may view only their own academic history. Advisors and Coordinators may view any advising student.
Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator
select an attended academic year and view the corresponding transcript
The transcript includes Winter, Spring, Summer, first-makeup and second-makeup results where applicable. An Advising Student may view only their own transcript.
Advising Student / Advisor / Coordinator
download the displayed transcript as a PDF
An Advising Student may download only their own transcript.
Advising Student
submit or update my scheduling preferences before the advising deadline

Preferences may include preferred or avoided days, preferred or avoided time ranges, preferred groups, desired days off and an optional note. The student may rank preferences by priority. Preferences are not guaranteed and cannot override mandatory courses, prerequisites, published offerings, capacity, timetable-clash rules, credit-hour limits or approved extra-hour rules.
Advisor / Coordinator
view an advising student's submitted scheduling preferences while creating or updating the draft schedule

Show the latest submitted preferences, their priority order and last update time. The Advisor or Coordinator may satisfy them when feasible but must preserve all academic and scheduling rules. A student who submitted no preferences may still receive a schedule.
Normal Student / Advising Student
connect my account to a supported third-party calendar using OAuth and synchronize my processed schedule

Support at least one provider, such as Google Calendar or Microsoft Outlook Calendar. The platform must not request or store the calendar password. Create recurring events for the teaching period using the university timezone. Each event includes course code and name, slot type, time, room and instructor when available.
